models_evaluated: eight LLM configurations (not named in the abstract)

links.outcome: Whether LLMs defer uncertain cases without over-deferring on supported or partially supported cases (over-refusal)
links.effect: All LLM configurations failed to retain the Partially Supported label in 83.3-100% of true Partially Supported cases. MTB-AuditAgent reduced over-refusal to 6.7% and reached 91.2% accuracy (95% CI 88.6-93.6%).
links.quote: Across eight large language model configurations, we identify pervasive over-refusal: all LLM configurations failed to retain the Partially Supported label in 83.3-100% of true Partially Supported cases, achieving high aggregate safety scores through label collapse rather than clinically calibrated reasoning.

unlisted_practices: Deterministic modular verification framework that separates evidence verification, missing-information detection, safety classification, and abstention
Two-oncologist annotation study to characterize expert disagreement on safety labels

screen.reason: The paper benchmarks LLM safety auditing in molecular tumor boards, identifies safety over-refusal/collapse, and evaluates a modular guardrail/audit agent (MTB-AuditAgent) separating evidence verification, missing-information detection, and abstention to improve clinical calibration.

primary.practice: multi-module safety auditing and abstention framework
